answer: Because the prism solution is checked at the pigment gate and logged, the bridge audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 23 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch thus pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. A farm of 261 pays that 83 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
